subject: chemistry
title: The Rock Cycle
welcome_lead: Rocks never truly die. They transform endlessly in a slow, planet-sized loop.
meta_desc: Trace the rock cycle in this KS3 chemistry adventure on igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic transformations.
final_note: You can now follow any rock around the planet's recycling system.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The rock cycle is the continuous transformation between igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks.

Rocks never disappear, they just change form.

A volcano erupts lava → it cools into igneous rock. Weathering breaks it up. Rivers carry pieces to the sea where they form layers → sedimentary rock.

If buried deep with heat and pressure → metamorphic rock. If it melts → back to magma.

Heat from Earth's interior drives the cycle. Plate movement, volcanoes and the weather all play a part.

Some rocks at your feet are billions of years old!
